profile.name: Derek Merrin
profile.bio: Derek Merrin served in the Ohio House from 2016 to 2025 and was elected leader of the House Republican Caucus. He was earlier a Waterville city council member and mayor, and he holds degrees from the University of Toledo and Bowling Green State University. He narrowly lost to Marcy Kaptur in 2024 and is the 2026 Republican nominee.

platform.point: Supports income tax cuts and a simpler, more transparent tax code.
Wants lower costs through price transparency and fewer regulations.
Supports photo ID requirements for voting.
Highlights his work passing constitutional carry in Ohio.
Points to his record expanding school choice.

economy.evidence: Led state income tax cuts and favors fewer regulations.

liberty.evidence: Championed constitutional carry (guns) and Down syndrome non-discrimination legislation related to abortion (abortion).

education.evidence: Expanded school choice as a legislator.

profile.notes: Liberty lowered from 80 to 50 because constitutional carry points toward individual choice on guns while his abortion-related record points the other way.

profile.name: Suzie Byrd
profile.bio: Suzie Byrd, of Enid, won the Democratic nomination for Oklahoma's 3rd Congressional District in June 2026. Raised in Hennessey and an Oklahoma State University graduate, she most recently worked as a reporter for the Enid News & Eagle and has owned or partnered in businesses in Oklahoma and Florida.
profile.notes: News summaries say her Facebook page prioritizes universal health care, affordable housing, immigration reform and education reform, but this could not be checked directly. No campaign website was found.

profile.name: Mike Mazzei
profile.current_role: Financial adviser and former Oklahoma Secretary of Budget
profile.bio: Mike Mazzei served in the Oklahoma Senate from 2004 to 2016, where he chaired the Finance Committee, and was Oklahoma's Secretary of Budget from 2019 to 2020 under Governor Kevin Stitt. He founded a financial coaching business and leads an investment management firm. He is based in Tulsa.

platform.point: Would eliminate property taxes for seniors and veterans.
Wants to close loopholes that let foreign adversaries control Oklahoma land.
Prioritises reading proficiency and accountability in schools.
Aims to attract investment and more high-paying jobs.
Promises transparency and fiscal discipline in state government.
Opposes abortion in all circumstances.

economy.evidence: Proposes phasing out the state income tax.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion in all circumstances (abortion); no other liberty issues found.

tech.evidence: Would end data-center tax breaks and regulate their water and power use.

profile.notes: The Commons photo is marked public domain only by an Oklahoma Legislative Service Bureau statement, not a named free license, so it was not used. Liberty score rests on abortion alone.

profile.name: Loran Ayles
profile.bio: Loran Ayles is a heavy equipment operator and the Republican nominee for Oregon's 3rd congressional district.
profile.notes: No campaign website or published issue positions were found; occupation comes from state filing records cited on Wikipedia.

profile.name: Patti Adair
profile.bio: Patti Adair has served as a Deschutes County commissioner since 2019 and is in her second term. She is a certified public accountant who grew up on a ranch in Heppner, Oregon, and returned to the state from California in 2014.

platform.point: Reduce the cost of living for working Oregonians and extend tax cuts on tips, overtime and Social Security.
Back law enforcement fully so local communities stay safe.
Manage natural resources through responsible stewardship.
Support business growth and entrepreneurs.
Prohibit insider trading by members of Congress.
Watch federal debt closely and keep spending accountable.

economy.evidence: Says Oregon taxes are among the highest and wants tip, overtime and Social Security tax cuts extended.

security.evidence: Pledges full support for law enforcement and cites increasing law enforcement funding as a commissioner.

profile.notes: Liberty left unscored because the cited priorities page does not address abortion or other social issues.

profile.name: Beth Farnham
profile.bio: Beth Farnham has worked as a credit analyst, administrative assistant and pharmacy technician and has served on a school board. A Baltimore native educated in public schools, she studied biology, French and secondary education, and she previously ran for PA-13.

platform.point: Create a national health program in federal law that covers all treatment and preventive care.
Protect personal decisions on abortion and birth control.
Reduce gun violence against children through measures such as universal background checks and red-flag orders.
Address rising living costs for working families, retirees, students and veterans.
Defend public education.

welfare.evidence: Wants a national healthcare program in federal law covering all treatment and preventive care.

liberty.evidence: Supports reproductive freedom on abortion and birth control and gun safety measures.

education.evidence: Campaign pledges to defend public education.

profile.notes: Her site mentions immigration reform without details; the location of her school board service was not stated.

profile.name: Glenn Thompson
profile.bio: Glenn "GT" Thompson has served in the U.S. House since 2009 (PA-5 until 2019, then PA-15) and has chaired the House Agriculture Committee since 2023. Born in Bellefonte and raised in Howard, he worked 28 years in therapeutic recreation and rehabilitation, including as a licensed nursing home administrator, and was a volunteer firefighter and EMT.

platform.point: Support farming as Pennsylvania's leading industry and a driver of rural economies.
Keep energy affordable and develop Marcellus Shale natural gas.
Expand access to affordable rural education and career and technical education.
Improve access, affordability and patient choice in rural health care.
Manage the Allegheny National Forest for multiple uses, including timber and energy.

liberty.evidence: Voted against the Respect for Marriage Act, while opposing arming teachers and supporting background check system funding (guns).

immigration.evidence: Was one of 30 Republicans to vote for the Farm Workforce Modernization Act in 2021.

energy.evidence: Prioritizes affordable energy and Marcellus Shale gas, opposed the WOTUS rule and is unsure how much humans drive climate change.

profile.name: Jessica Arriaga
profile.bio: Jessica Arriaga is a North Philadelphia native who has worked for more than 20 years in operating rooms and in community health care. She is running as a first-time candidate.

platform.point: Ease rising living costs for working Philadelphia families.
Make neighborhoods safer.
Widen economic and educational opportunity in the district.

profile.notes: The campaign site names broad themes but no specific policy positions.
